title: The Student Revolt in France Spreads : Moving Forward with Rage and Solidarity
content:
October 17 marked one of the fiercest days of mass protest in recent French history. Scenes of ferocious resistance unfolded throughout the day, not only in Paris but in 


Bordeaux

, 


Dijon

, 

Marseille

, 

Nancy

, and dozens of other cities across the country. Some observers have described the day’s events as 

more explosive

 than the 

Yellow Vest movement

 of 2018-19—and the rebellion shows no sign of slowing.




How did we get here? Courageous high school students 

have been protesting for weeks

 against abominable conditions in schools, the rise of the extreme right, and the bleak prospects they face in a world dominated by technocrats and tech barons. Alongside growing anti-government protests from 

Albania

, 

Italy

, 

Spain

, and beyond in recent days, the French student rebellions may herald the emergence of a new wave of global struggle.




In this article, our correspondent from Paris explains the context behind the youth rebellion, tracks the movement’s growth over the two weeks leading up to October 17 and the government’s failed attempts to repress or to pacify it, and clarifies the stakes moving forward.




Stay tuned for a full report on the uprising of October 17 and the ongoing rebellions across France and beyond.

title: French Youth Take the Streets against a Bleak Future : A Report
content:
This past week, thousands of teenagers have taken the streets of France, clashing with police as they demonstrate against the deplorable conditions in their high schools and a rapidly collapsing future. This is a promising sign, shifting attention from the seemingly unstoppable rise of the extreme right to the question of what people can do on a grassroots basis to defend themselves. Our correspondents in Paris explore the situation in detail.







Another unprecedented summer of record 

heatwaves

, 

droughts

, and 

wildfires

 throughout Europe underlines the desperate situation we are all facing today, while politicians of all stripes and their techno-industrial sponsors continue to turn a blind eye, forcing us down the path to catastrophe in the name of progress.




Hoping to turn the page on these environmental disasters, the French government has hurriedly shifted focus to other priorities. The coming months represent a crucial transition for Emmanuel Macron and his government, as they will bring Macron’s second term to a close, opening a new political era in France. Candidates are already battling to succeed Macron in power at the beginning of May 2027.
